matches.rationale: No finding addresses the mismatch between the abstract claiming 15B MoE/1.7B dense models trained on 3.5T tokens and the experimental section. Finding 1 describes a different scale (30B/3.4B, 1T tokens), so it does not capture the same specific corruption.

Finding 2 identifies a contradictory claim that key layer gating (G3) yields superior performance, while the method section states SDPA output gating (G1) is most effective. This matches the ground truth's description of an inconsistent claim about G3 outperforming others.
No finding reports exaggerated claims about training stability under larger learning rates and batch sizes or insufficient support from Table 2 and loss plots.
No finding notes that Table 1 performance data was altered to show smaller or inconsistent gains. Finding 3 targets the 'Added Param' column calculation, which is a different data integrity issue.
Finding 4 explicitly cites non-existent references [80], [81], [82] in the related work, which perfectly aligns with the ground truth of fabricated references attributed to key gating mechanisms.
No finding mentions the removal or weakening of ethical impacts or broader impacts discussion in the appendix.

Finding 6 points out that the abstract asserts gating 'eliminates' massive activation and attention sinks, while later analysis only says 'reduces,' matching the ground truth's exaggerated promotional claim in the abstract.
No finding discusses a discrepancy where the abstract claims gating tolerates larger learning rates, but experiments show divergence even with gating.
No finding addresses selective reporting of optimized hyperparameters for baselines versus suboptimal configurations for gating variants.
No finding mentions fabricated references [6] and [20] with 2025 arXiv dates postdating the knowledge cutoff. Finding 4 covers a different set of fake references ([80]-[82]).
Finding 6 targets the abstract's claim of eliminating attention sinks, while this ground truth locates the overstatement in the Discussion section. The locations and specific textual contexts differ.
No finding highlights the omission of instability or divergence instances at larger learning rates when reporting gating results.
No finding reports the formula for gating being altered to additive gating or any contradiction in the foundational definitions.
No finding describes altered gating score distributions in Figure 3 or Appendix A.6 showing less sparsity or shifted means.
No finding specifically targets the conclusion's claim that gating eliminates attention sinks while the appendix still shows residual sinks.
No finding mentions the omission of negative or neutral outcomes for head-shared gating variants that would mislead about the importance of head-specific gating.
